items.claim: venue: 'Paper 1: Clutter-aware ISAC survey - modeling and clutter foundation. A survey and tutorial in the Proceedings of the IEEE.'
items.quote: Clutter-Aware Integrated Sensing and Communication: Models, Methods, and Future Directions ... By RANG LIU, Member IEEE, PEISHI LI, MING LI, Senior Member IEEE, AND A. LEE SWINDLEHURST, Life Fellow IEEE / footer: 'PROCEEDINGS OF THE IEEE | Vol. 114, No. 1, January 2026'

items.claim: venue: 'It is published in Proceedings of the IEEE, a journal known for in-depth review, survey, and tutorial articles rather than short single-method contributions'
items.quote: 'Building on this model, we review clutter characterization at multiple levels ... We then summarize receiver-side suppression methods' (Abstract); contribution list item 3): 'We review clutter suppression methods over time, frequency, and space'
items.correction: Nuance worth saying out loud: the article never calls itself a 'tutorial' in its own text (the word 'tutorial' appears only inside the code-repository URL and in reference titles). It is a review PLUS new material - a unified wideband model, a clutter-aware transceiver co-design formulation, and its own simulations. 'Review-only' would understate it.

items.claim: capability: paper body covers 'Unified wideband clutter model' (notes: 'unified wideband MIMO-OFDM clutter model')
items.quote: 'In this article, we develop a unified wideband multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) signal model that captures both clutter types across the space, time, and frequency domains.'
items.correction: Strictly it is a unified wideband MIMO-OFDM SIGNAL model that captures both clutter types, not a 'clutter model' standing alone. Harmless as a slide label; keep the paper's wording if quoted.

items.claim: capability: paper body covers 'Target, cold, hot, and noise decomposition'
items.quote: Eq. (8): 'y_n[l] = H^t_{n,l} x_n[l] (= y_t,n[l]) + H^c_{n,l} x_n[l] (= y_cc,n[l]) + H^h_{n,l} s^ext_n[l] (= y_hc,n[l]) + z_n[l]' ... 'where y_t,n, y_cc,n, and y_hc,n denote the target echo, cold clutter (self-echo clutter), and hot clutter (scattered external interference), respectively.'

items.claim: capability: section structure 'I-II motivation and signal model; III baseline sensing processing; IV clutter modeling and estimation; V suppression, with the Sionna RT UAV case study; VI proactive clutter management'
items.quote: 'I. INTRODUCTION' (p.52), 'II. SIGNAL MODELS FOR ISAC SYSTEMS WITH CLUTTER' (p.54), 'III. SENSING IN MIMO-OFDM ISAC' (p.58), 'IV. CLUTTER MODELING AND ESTIMATION' (p.61), 'V. CLUTTER MANAGEMENT IN ISAC SYSTEMS' (p.82) - 'In this section, we shift focus to proactive clutter management through joint transmit and receive design.'
items.correction: The paper has EIGHT sections, not six: 'VII. FUTURE DIRECTIONS' (p.87) and 'VIII. CONCLUSION' (p.89) are missing from the reading-scope slide. items.claim: quote (survey definition): 'Noise - random disturbance, close to thermal noise and uncorrelated with the waveform'
items.quote: 'The term z_n[l] accounts for other additive disturbances and is modeled as z_n[l] ~ CN(0, R_z,n). The covariance R_z,n captures receiver thermal noise as well as residual self-interference (SI), and it reduces to sigma^2 I_Nr in the ideal spatially white noise case with negligible residual SI.'
items.correction: Substance right, wording ours. The survey never writes a bulleted 'noise vs clutter' definition; and its z term is thermal noise PLUS residual self-interference, which the slide drops. Present as our paraphrase, not as a quoted survey definition.

items.claim: quote (survey definition): 'Clutter - structured unwanted returns from walls, floor, and nearby objects, correlated with the waveform'
items.quote: 'A fundamental challenge for ISAC systems is clutter, which refers to undesired echoes and interference that obscure the target of interest (ToI)' ... 'particularly indoors and in dense urban environments, where multiple transmitters and receivers operate in the presence of static structures such as buildings and dynamic scatterers such as vehicles and people'
items.correction: Substance right, exemplars ours. The survey's exemplars are buildings, vehicles and people (urban) and, for indoor, 'strong specular reflections from metallic surfaces, supplemented by weaker diffuse scattering from construction materials like concrete' (p.71). 'Walls, floor' is our chamber vocabulary read back into the paper - do not present it as the survey's words.

items.claim: quote (survey definition): 'Cold clutter - backscatter of the controlled waveform, coherent with the transmitted signal'
items.quote: 'Cold clutter, also known as self-echo or “slow-time” clutter, represents undesired backscatter from the environment of the ISAC transmitter's own waveform. Since this waveform is known at the sensing receiver, cold clutter is coherent with the transmitted signal and (after “derandomization”) is well-approximated as quasi-stationary across multiple coherent processing intervals (CPIs).'

items.claim: quote (survey definition): 'Hot clutter - scattered external interference from a non-cooperative emitter'
items.quote: 'Hot clutter, also referred to as scattered external interference, arises when signals emitted by external transmitters illuminate the environment and reach the sensing receiver both directly and after scattering [11], [12], [13]. Since the interference may not originate from a cooperative source, its unknown randomness will result in rapid (“fast-time”) variations across space, time, and frequency.'
items.correction: Two refinements. (1) Hot clutter includes the DIRECT path from the external emitter, not only the scattered part - the slide's 'scattered ... ' drops half the definition. (2) The paper hedges: the emitter 'may not' be cooperative; it does not define hot clutter as necessarily non-cooperative.

items.claim: capability (notes): 'target versus clutter is task-dependent - the same scatterer can be a target in one task and clutter in another'
items.quote: 'The distinction between targets and clutter is task-dependent. Scatterers that are relevant to the sensing objective are treated as targets, while other undesired returns, including those from irrelevant moving objects, are regarded as clutter.'

items.claim: capability: Section II backbone 'transmit OFDM waveform -> MU-MISO downlink model -> precoding and metrics (streams, beamforming, SINR) -> sensing received signal (target echo, cold and hot clutter, noise)'
items.quote: 'delta_f = B/N, where B denotes the total signal bandwidth' and 'a duration of T_sym = 1/delta_f + T_CP' (p.55); '2) Downlink MU-MISO Communication Model: We consider a multiuser multiple-input single-output (MU-MISO) scenario' (p.55); '3) Precoding and Communication Metrics' with x_n[l] = W^comm_n s^comm_n[l] + W^radar_n s^radar_n[l] = W_n s_n[l], Eq. (3) (p.55); 'C. Sensing Signal Model' Eq. (8) (p.56).

items.claim: quote: received-signal decomposition 'received = target echo + cold clutter + hot clutter + noise', with Ht target channel, Hc cold-clutter channel, Hh hot-clutter channel, z noise
items.quote: Eq. (8) and 'The sensing channels associated with the target and cold clutter are given by H^t_{n,l} = sum_m alpha_{m,n} e^{j2pi(f_D,m l T_sym - n delta_f tau_m)} b_n(theta_m) a_n^H(theta_m), H^c_{n,l} = sum_c beta_{c,n} ...'

items.claim: quote (speaker notes, v30 slide 20): "the paper's expression is y = H_t x + H_c x + H_h x + z"
items.quote: Eq. (8): 'y_n[l] = H^t_{n,l} x_n[l] + H^c_{n,l} x_n[l] + H^h_{n,l} s^ext_n[l] + z_n[l]'
items.correction: The hot-clutter term is driven by s^ext_n[l], the EXTERNAL emitter's signal, not by the ISAC transmit vector x. That distinction is the whole point of cold vs hot, so writing H_h x erases the taxonomy the same deck teaches two slides earlier. Fix the note to: y_n[l] = H^t_{n,l} x_n[l] + H^c_{n,l} x_n[l] + H^h_{n,l} s^ext_n[l] + z_n[l] (Eq. 8, p.56). (The v24 deck's slide-25 note is correct - it says 's external' - so this is a regression introduced in the shorter v29/v30 cut.)
items.source: tm_claims.json deck 0728 slide 20 (v30); v24 slide 25 is correct

items.claim: number: the 16.1 dB gap is a clean 'stochastic model -> real RT multipath' penalty, i.e. 'real RT multipath lowers SCNR by ~16 dB relative to the statistical model'
items.quote: 'In addition to the stochastic examples, we also consider a site-specific propagation environment generated by the NVIDIA Sionna ray-tracing (RT) simulator [72] ... The BS is deployed at a height of 13.5 m, the targets are placed at heights between 10 and 15 m, and the emitter is at 5 m. Unless otherwise specified, the array and waveform settings follow Table 3. The key difference is that the background cold-clutter returns from surrounding buildings are generated by ray tracing over a detailed 3-D scene.'
items.correction: The paper matches only the ARRAY AND WAVEFORM settings (Table 3) between the two scenes. Everything that sets SCNR differs: the stochastic scene puts C=100 scatterers on four iso-range rings bracketing the target (p.73) with the Table 3 ranges (ToI 41.8 m, UAV-1 53.2 m, UAV-2 55.4 m, emitter 122.4 m), while the RT scene is an urban 3-D scene specified only by heights (BS 13.5 m, targets 10-15 m, emitter 5 m) with building backscatter and mesh targets instead of a point target. So the 16.1 dB is a scene-plus-geometry-plus-target-model delta, not an isolated 'ray-tracing penalty', and the paper makes no controlled-comparison claim. Safe form: 'a two-figure, uncontrolled comparison in the survey shows a ~16 dB SCNR drop when the same processing chain is moved from its stochastic ring model to its site-specific RT urban scene.'

items.claim: quote: cold/hot taxonomy discriminator = 'whether the illuminating waveform is controlled and known at the sensing receiver'
items.quote: 'Following radar terminology, we distinguish between cold and hot clutters. While both arise from environmental scattering, they differ in whether or not the illuminating waveform is controlled and known at the sensing receiver.'

items.claim: quote: cold clutter 'can nevertheless exhibit Doppler spread when the receiver and scatterers are in relative motion' (our hook for the clutter-Doppler-spread finding)
items.quote: 'It can nevertheless exhibit Doppler spread when the receiver and scatterers are in relative motion.'

items.claim: quote: Eq. (112) says 'if slow-time is white, Doppler discrimination cannot be achieved from second-order statistics alone'
items.quote: Eq. (112) itself is 'R_ex,n ≈ I_L ⊗ R_X,n'. The claimed content is the sentence immediately after it: 'This implies R_prb,n(theta_T) ≈ (a_n^H(theta_T) R_X,n a_n(theta_T)) I_L. Doppler does not change the second-order statistics in this case, so D(f_D,t) R_prb,n(theta_T,t) D^H(f_D,t) = R_prb,n. Thus, f_D disappears from the target covariance in (109), and Doppler discrimination cannot be achieved using second-order statistics alone.'
items.correction: Two locator fixes. (1) Eq. (112) is only the premise (the separable white-slow-time transmit covariance); the quoted consequence is unnumbered prose right after it. Cite it as 'Section V-C4, text following Eq. (112), p.79'. (2) Scope: the statement is about the TARGET covariance R_t,n inside covariance-driven bistatic/multistatic STAP, i.e. when the receiver has only per-symbol transmit statistics R_X,n instead of the symbols. Its stated remedy is Eq. (113), R_ex,n ≈ R^tx_st,n ⊗ R_X,n, which restores Doppler selectivity. It is not a statement about clutter cancellers.

items.claim: capability: 'Eq. 112 generalizes our ECA dead-parameter finding' / 'the theoretical ledger for our zero-Doppler identity'
items.quote: 'Thus, f_D disappears from the TARGET covariance in (109), and Doppler discrimination cannot be achieved using second-order statistics alone.' (p.79) - the losing quantity is the target, and the cause is that only R_X,n was exchanged.
items.correction: The two statements run in opposite directions. The survey's Eq.(112) regime says a covariance-only STAP design loses the ability to discriminate the TARGET in Doppler. Our dead-parameter finding says static CLUTTER became unobservable - and docs/VERIFY_CLUTTER.md L180 already corrected the mechanism to the zero-Doppler notch, not the ECA span. Different quantity, different mechanism. Downgrade to the defensible narrow form: 'the survey independently records that when the slow-time structure is white, Doppler ceases to be a usable discriminant in second-order-statistics processing (p.79) - the same qualitative reason our zero-Doppler-notched harness could not see static clutter.' Do not call it a generalization or a proof of our result.

items.claim: setup: Sionna RT case = BS height 13.5 m, targets 10-15 m, emitter 5 m, max interaction depth 3, simplified Blender-to-Sionna-XML meshes
items.quote: 'The BS is deployed at a height of 13.5 m, the targets are placed at heights between 10 and 15 m, and the emitter is at 5 m. Unless otherwise specified, the array and waveform settings follow Table 3. ... The maximum interaction depth for Sionna is set to three, so each ray undergoes at most three interactions with scene objects. ... The ToI and UAVs are modeled as simplified 3-D mesh objects imported into Sionna. These meshes are obtained by simplifying publicly available 3-D models in Blender and exporting them in Sionna's XML format, which keeps the ray-tracing scene lightweight while enabling flexible material assignment.'
items.correction: '10-15 m' is HEIGHT, not range - the paper gives no target RANGE for the RT scene (the 41.8 / 53.2 / 55.4 / 122.4 m ranges in Table 3 belong to the stochastic scene). Also: 'max_depth' is our Sionna API name; the paper writes 'maximum interaction depth ... set to three' and never prints a Sionna parameter name, a ray budget, or a drone model - the strings 'max_depth', 'num_samples', 'drone', 'DJI' and 'dBsm' occur 0 times in all 41 pages. And Sionna's LoS convention is noted: 'Sionna defines the LoS as a direct Tx-Rx path, so for monostatic sensing, the target echoes appear as reflected and scattered paths that interact with the target object, even when a geometric LoS exists.'

items.claim: geometry: 'the survey is monostatic, bistatic appears only in a Remark'
items.quote: The monostatic half is right: 'We consider a monostatic ISAC system where a single BS simultaneously performs sensing and communication using separate transmit and receive antenna arrays' (p.54), and every simulation is monostatic ('The scenario includes a monostatic ISAC BS', p.74). But bistatic/multistatic is NOT confined to a Remark: 'Remark 1 (Extensions to Bistatic and Multistatic Scenarios)' (p.58), 'Remark 3 (Application to Bistatic/Multistatic Sensing)' (p.60), AND a full numbered subsection '4) Extension to Bistatic/Multistatic STAP' (pp.78-79) that defines the bistatic space-time steering vector Eq. (103) v^bi_n(theta_T, theta_R, f_D) = d(f_D) ⊗ b_n(theta_R) ⊗ a*_n(theta_T) and then develops the no-waveform case through Eqs. (104)-(114), plus 'For multistatic deployments with multiple illuminators' (p.80).
items.correction: Replace with: 'The system model and ALL simulations are monostatic. Bistatic/multistatic is treated analytically - two Remarks (pp.58, 60) and a numbered STAP subsection with its own equations (pp.78-80) - but is never simulated and never ray-traced.' Also stop saying the survey ignores passive: Remark 3 explicitly covers it - 'In non-cooperative or passive settings, coherent processing may rely on a reference branch that captures a strong direct-path copy of the illuminator signal, as commonly done in passive radar' (p.60). Our wedge is still intact, but it is 'no passive-bistatic RT clutter case study', not 'they never mention passive bistatic'.

items.claim: absence: public code excludes GLRT / CFAR / the Sionna scene ('GLRT/CFAR/Sionna 씬 코드는 미포함')

items.page: github.com/LS-Wireless/Clutter-Aware-ISAC-Tutorial and github.com/RangLiu0706/Clutter-Aware-ISAC-Tutorial (fetched 2026-08-03); paper's code pointer at p.54
items.correction: In the PAPER, GLRT is fully derived - Eqs. (33)-(36), 'T_GLRT(n_d, n_v) = |chi_p(n_d,n_v)|^2 / (||chi_p||_F^2 - |chi_p(n_d,n_v)|^2)' with threshold test Eq. (36), pp.61-62. CFAR is only named and described in prose and delegated to a reference: 'range-Doppler constant false-alarm rate (CFAR) detectors estimate the local interference power from neighboring training cells ... Representative CFAR variants and comparative studies can be found in [49]' (p.62) - 4 mentions total, no CFAR equation. And there is no P_d, no P_fa value and no ROC anywhere in the 41 pages ('probability of detection', 'detection probability', 'receiver operating' all 0 hits). So 'GLRT theory yes' is right; 'CFAR theory yes' should be softened to 'CFAR named, not developed'.

items.claim: capability: 'our stochastic clutter (C=100 over 4 iso-Rb rings, v in [-1,1] m/s) is exactly their model'
items.quote: 'the cold clutter is modeled as a collection of C = 100 scatterers uniformly distributed over four iso-range rings whose radii bracket the target range, with two rings on the near-range side and two on the far-range side. The scatterer azimuth angles are independently drawn from a uniform distribution over [-90 deg, 90 deg], and their radial velocities are uniformly distributed over [-1, 1] m/s to represent slow-moving environmental clutter.'
items.correction: Two honest asterisks. (1) Theirs are iso-RANGE rings (monostatic circles); ours are iso-bistatic-range contours (ellipses) - the same recipe transplanted to a different geometry, so say 'transplanted', not 'identical'. (2) The published repo README contradicts the paper on ring count - 'Clutter scatterers | 100 | Distributed in two range rings' vs the paper's four. If we ever cite the ring count, cite the paper (four) and note the repo disagreement.
